criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Users (marine scientists, conservation) and rationale are identified and referenced via footnotes. However, mission goals, objectives and requirements are not stated quantitatively (no orbit, sensor, resolution or coverage requirements), and the 'what it will do' is vague. Some claims are loosely supported (e.g. 'Oceans 30% more acidic' is an overstatement of pH change). Adequate rather than accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
A newer technology designed by ASU Professor Greg Asner has been used in Hawaii to detect colour/tone changes to the seafloor

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart with dependencies, deadlines and status is given, with task descriptions and information sources. Contingency is implicit via 'ongoing' and cutting strategies, but not explicit. Plan is reasonably robust and tied to the mission narrative, though information sources are only a list of links and the link to mission is thin.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
Final design and simulation should be completed by the end of week 9.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is mostly reading and tutorials. No orbit, launch or coverage calculations or STK simulation results are presented, so there is no technical content demonstrating design progress. Minor work completed only.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and logical sections with footnotes. Some inconsistencies: Gantt figure referenced 'on the next page' with a caption-less image, bullet task list is informal, footnote numbering is in text but Useful Links are not tied to in-text citations, and 'Coral reefs' section is awkward. Writing is generally readable with minor grammar issues ('nurture'). Adequate overall.

evidence.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution

technical_issues.issue: 'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' misstates the pH change (about 30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration); needs precise wording.
Bleaching is attributed to acidification, whereas the main driver is thermal stress; the causal chain is inaccurate.
No space-segment design content (orbit altitude, inclination, launch vehicle) is applied despite R2; no software selection (R3) is stated.

overall: Good motivation and a clear Gantt plan, but the report lacks space-segment technical content, explicit software choice, and quantified mission requirements. Some scientific statements are inaccurate. Preliminary progress is mainly reading and tutorials, so it is below the level needed for full marks.

feedback.summary: You have built a clear, well-motivated mission concept around monitoring coral reef bleaching, and your Gantt chart gives the project a sensible timeline with dependencies and deadlines. Your mission goals and user groups are identified and referenced. To strengthen the report, state your requirements quantitatively, add space-segment design content and early calculations, and correct the scientific statements on ocean acidification and bleaching. Your Preliminary Progress section needs results you can interpret, not only tutorials.
next_steps: Restate your mission goals as quantified requirements (for example, revisit time, spatial resolution, coverage area and latency), and link each requirement to a named user need.

Add early space-segment design work: choose an orbit altitude and inclination, a launch vehicle option and a software tool (such as STK), and show a first coverage or pass calculation with a brief interpretation.
Correct the acidification wording to describe the pH change accurately, and state that thermal stress is the main driver of bleaching, with acidification as a secondary concern.

criteria.C1: You identify the users (marine and conservation scientists) and explain why near-real-time monitoring matters, with supporting references such as the Asner Hawaii work. To reach the Accomplished level, state specific mission goals, objectives and requirements, such as orbit, sensor, resolution and coverage, and tie each mission function directly to a user need. Correct the overstated acidification claim so your rationale is precise.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart shows task dependencies, deadlines and status, and your task descriptions and information sources give the plan credibility. To reach the Accomplished level, make contingencies and project variations explicit rather than implied, and explain more clearly why the plan's structure follows from the mission concept. Connect your information sources to specific tasks rather than listing them.
criteria.C3: You have completed STK tutorials and reviewed the Asner monitoring system, which shows that you are building familiarity with the tools. To reach the Good level, present preliminary technical results, such as orbit or coverage calculations or early STK outputs, with a brief interpretation of what they show and whether they keep you on track for completion.
criteria.C4: The report has clear headings, a logical section sequence and footnotes, and it is generally readable. To reach the Accomplished level, make in-text citations match the reference list, including the Useful Links, and apply consistent formatting to figures and tables. Tighten the informal bullet task list and the awkward Coral Reefs wording, and proofread for minor grammar issues.
